author: Las Vegas City Wire
title: Dina Titus voices concerns over SCOTUS decision and promotes key legislation
text:
Dina Titus, U.S. Representative for Nevada's 1stcongressional district | Official U.S. House Headshot
Dina Titus, U.S. Representative for Nevada's 1stcongressional district | Official U.S. House Headshot
Dina Titus, a member of the U.S. Congress representing Nevada’s 1st district, has expressed her views on recent political developments through a series of tweets. Serving since 2013, Titus has been an active voice in legislative matters and public policy discussions.
On July 9, 2025, Titus commented on a Supreme Court decision, stating that it would "allow @POTUS to completely wreck the federal government." She voiced concerns that this decision could hinder public servants from providing essential services to Americans and strain available resources. "This #SCOTUS decision will allow @POTUS to completely wreck the federal government. This will prevent our hardworking public servants from delivering assistance to everyday Americans, depleting resources and putting more of a strain on services."
In another tweet later that day, Titus highlighted the importance of extreme heat planning and mitigation. She announced her collaboration with Representative Mike Lawler in recognizing National Extreme Heat Awareness Week. She also advocated for her proposed legislation aimed at modernizing FEMA's response to extreme weather events. "Extreme heat planning and mitigation save lives. That is why I am joining @RepMikeLawler in recognizing National Extreme Heat Awareness Week. This is the perfect time for Congress to take up my Extreme Weather and Heat Response Modernization Act which would expand @FEMA’s"
Titus also emphasized the urgency of passing the FAIR BET Act, thanking various media outlets for their support in raising awareness about the issue. She encouraged continued efforts to promote this legislative initiative. "We’re getting the word out that Congress needs to pass the FAIR BET Act as soon as possible."
Dina Titus was born in Thomasville, Georgia in 1950 and currently resides in Las Vegas. She graduated from College of William & Mary with a BA in 1970.
